hero.title: Dira AR Pathfinder
hero.subtitle: An offline-first spatial guidance platform that fuses map tiles with agentic vision for landmark-aware navigation.

origin.pullQuote: Navigation becomes human when the map understands what people actually see.
paragraphs: Dira AR Pathfinder was initiated to solve real-world wayfinding failure in low-connectivity environments where conventional map apps degrade quickly. The project focuses on practical, grounded navigation for users who need reliable guidance without always-on internet.

The system combines offline map data with camera-driven contextual interpretation, enabling route assistance that references landmarks and visual surroundings instead of only coordinate turn-by-turn abstractions.

architecture.title: Offline Geospatial + Vision Overlay Stack
architecture.description: A TypeScript-first architecture that merges offline routing, camera scene analysis, and AR overlay rendering.
architecture.narrative: The architecture separates spatial responsibilities into route graph computation, localization updates, and rendering orchestration. Offline map assets are treated as first-class dependencies, allowing deterministic fallback when networks are unavailable. Vision-layer interpretation adds contextual hints that are converted into stable overlay cues, while route-state management guards against jittery re-rendering in movement-heavy sessions.

hardParts.title: Stabilizing AR Guidance Under Noisy Localization
hardParts.description: The hardest challenge was preventing overlay drift and direction jitter during real-time movement.
hardParts.narrative: Raw sensor and vision updates produced inconsistent headings and frequent micro-corrections that damaged usability. The solution introduced smoothing windows, route snapping thresholds, and state-aware re-render controls so overlays changed only when confidence passed defined boundaries. This significantly improved user trust in directional guidance.
